subject.title: [Feature]: Show session and requester context in macOS exec approval popup

question: Which requester identity fields may the macOS exec-approval popup disclose beyond a sanitized session identity?
rationale: The Session parity gap is source-proven, but raw channel targets, account IDs, sender identifiers, and thread IDs cross a privacy-sensitive desktop display boundary that current policy and history do not define.

options.title: Ship session identity first
options.body: Add a sanitized Session row now and defer richer requester fields until their disclosure contract is separately approved.

options.title: Approve selected requester fields
options.body: Define redaction and trust rules for specific Channel, Sender, and Thread fields, then implement them with the Session row.

options.title: Retain current metadata
options.body: Keep the popup limited to command, agent, host, and policy context and decline the additional identity surface.

recommendation.title: Ship session identity first
recommendation.body: Add a sanitized Session row now and defer richer requester fields until their disclosure contract is separately approved.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior review already framed the native parity fix versus richer privacy-sensitive context, and this person is connected to the native app baseline.
